_comment: Party-menu mon-icon animation schedule, banked for the future engine wiring rung (docs/party-menu-notes.md). Source: reference/pokeemerald/src/pokemon_icon.c + src/party_menu.c, cross-checked against dense stride-1 oracle captures of battle1-turn15-dense.json ticks 20064-20260, PLUS (this session) a direct RAM probe (tools/probe/dump-party-icon-bounce.py) of every gSprites[] slot's x/y/x2/y2/animNum/animCmdIndex/animDelayCounter over the same window.

mechanism.bitmapFrames: Each icon sprite is 32x32, backed by a 32x64 icon.png (2 stacked 32x32 bitmap frames: top=frame0, bottom=frame1). UpdateMonIconFrame (pokemon_icon.c:1230) alternates the OAM tile data between the two frames once sprite->animDelayCounter reaches 0.
mechanism.speedTable: 5 anim scripts (pokemon_icon.c sAnim_0..sAnim_4), each just frame0<->frame1 at a fixed per-frame delay D_N: animNum 0=6 ticks/frame (fastest), 1=8, 2=14, 3=22, 4=29-but-both-entries-are-frame0 (no BITMAP change, but see hopModel below - the POSITION still hops).
mechanism.speedSelection: In the party menu specifically, UpdatePartyMonHPBar -> UpdateHPBar (party_menu.c:3951) calls SetPartyHPBarSprite(spriteId, animNum) where animNum = 0/1/2/3/4 for HP_BAR_FULL/GREEN/YELLOW/RED/(fainted-or-egg default) - i.e. the icon's bounce SPEED is driven by its own mon's current HP-bar color, not a global clock. Each icon sprite carries its own animDelayCounter/animCmdIndex - independent per icon, not synced.
mechanism.iconSpriteCoordConvention: RAM-confirmed this session: struct Sprite's x/y (include/sprite.h +0x20/+0x22) are the icon's OAM *center* coordinate for a 32x32 sprite, not its top-left. Screen top-left = (x + x2 - 16, y + y2 - 16). This base x/y is constant per icon for the whole turn (16,40)=ONIX / (104,18)=MAGBY / (104,42)=BAYLEEF - only x2/y2 change.
mechanism.deselectedFixedOffset: AnimateSelectedPartyIcon(spriteId, animNum=0) (party_menu.c:3978-4001, called on deselect): if sprite->x==16 (box1/'current' slot only) sets x2=0,y2=-4; every OTHER box sets x2=-4,y2=0. This is a PERMANENT fixed offset (callback becomes the plain SpriteCB_UpdatePartyMonIcon, which never touches y2/x2 again) - RAM-confirmed for MAGBY/BAYLEEF (unselected the whole turn) and for ONIX after its own tick-20191 deselect.
mechanism.hopModel: AnimateSelectedPartyIcon(spriteId, animNum=1) sets x2=0,y2=0 and switches the callback to SpriteCB_BouncePartyMonIcon (party_menu.c:4003-4014): `animCmd = UpdateMonIconFrame(sprite); if (animCmd) sprite->y2 = (animCmd & 1) ? -3 : 1;`. x2 stays 0 for the whole time the icon is selected (RAM-confirmed for both ONIX and MAGBY while selected - no horizontal hop, only vertical). y2 alternates -3/+1, changing only on an actual UpdateMonIconFrame frame-advance event (not every tick) - RAM-derived exact timing for animNum N (per-frame delay D_N from speedTable): y2=-3 holds for D_N+1 ticks, then y2=+1 holds for D_N+2 ticks, full period = 2*D_N+3. The asymmetry is sMonIconAnims's own trailing JUMP(0) command: it silently re-arms animCmdIndex one tick before the next visible frame copy without itself touching y2, stretching the +1 half by exactly 1 tick relative to the -3 half. Verified via RAM for ONIX (animNum 4, D=29): consecutive flip ticks 20114(-3)->20144(+1)->20175(-3), deltas 30/31 = D+1/D+2 exactly. Verified for MAGBY post-select (animNum 0, D=6): flip ticks 20195(+1)->20203(-3)->20212(+1)->20220(-3) (unperturbed by the tick 20205-20207 stall, see renderLag below), deltas 8/7/8 = D+2/D+1/D+2 exactly.
mechanism.renderLag: BISECTED this session (not assumed): the y2/frame-bitmap effects of UpdateMonIconFrame's own delay-driven redraw lag the RAM's own bookkeeping by exactly 1 tick in the rendered PNG - e.g. ONIX's y2 flips to +1 in RAM at tick 20144, but the oracle's PNG capture at tick 20144 still shows -3; the flip is only visible from PNG tick 20145 on (confirmed the same way for MAGBY's frame0->1 flip: RAM-tick 20150/20212, visible from PNG-tick 20151/20213). This is a GBA-generic one-VBlank pipeline delay between a sprite struct write and its OAM/VRAM copy taking visible effect - the SAME class of lag this run's PROGRESS ledger has bisected for other mechanisms (turn13/14 bounce drivers), just newly confirmed for this one. By contrast, the SELECT/DESELECT position jump (x2 -4<->0, the fixed-offset swap above) has ZERO lag: DOWN pressed at trace-tick 20191 and the RAM x2/y2 swap is visible in the SAME tick's own state read - confirmed because that swap is applied synchronously by AnimateSelectedPartyIcon on the input-handling tick itself, with no delay counter involved, unlike the ongoing bounce.
mechanism.statusIconOverlap: A separate always-created per-slot sprite (`sSpriteTemplate_StatusIcons`, `CreatePartyMonStatusSprite`/`UpdatePartyMonAilmentGfx`, party_menu.c:4184-4221) sits at `menuBox->spriteCoords[4,5]`, hidden (`invisible=TRUE`) only when `GetMonAilment(mon)==AILMENT_NONE`. RAM-probed this session at tick 20070: gSprites slot 9 (an 8x8, OBJ-palette-0/VRAM-tile-0 sprite positioned right at BAYLEEF's own icon's bottom-right corner) is in-use and NOT invisible, i.e. BAYLEEF is carrying a status ailment this turn and this indicator is drawn on top of the icon there. Its palette+tile content ((248,240,152)/(216,216,112)/(240,80,40)/(160,88,80) in 15-bit RAM, matching the oracle's 24-bit expansion of the same tick's actual pixels EXACTLY) is the root cause of the long-standing 'BAYLEEF corner residual' - see docs/party-menu-notes.md's newest section. Not extractor-side: the mon-icon bitmap/palette/position are all correct; this is a genuinely separate, correctly-behaving UI element outside the icon asset's own scope.

ONIX.note: RESOLVED this session: the selected-icon y2 hop DOES fire for ONIX (fainted) exactly per hopModel above - RAM-confirmed y2 alternates -3/+1 with period 61 (=2*29+3) the whole time ONIX is selected (ticks 20064-20190). The earlier 'zero pixel change over 121 ticks' claim was an artifact of not sampling a phase-changed tick; a fresh pixel cross-check (oracle PNGs at ticks 20070/20120 [-3] vs 20150 [+1]) shows real, visible pixel movement. sAnim_4's own frame table has both entries pointing at frame0, so the BITMAP never changes, only the y2 position. Deselects at tick 20191 (same tick as the DOWN press, 0 render lag) to the permanent y2=-4 fixed offset.

MAGBY.note: verified: reference-extracted frame0/frame1 bitmap+palette matches oracle pixels almost exactly at its deselected anchor (84,2) - diff 2px (frame0)/8px (frame1) out of ~300-400 opaque pixels (residual not chased, sub-1%, unrelated to the statusIconOverlap corner). Selected at tick 20191 (same tick as the DOWN press, 0 render lag: x2 jumps -4->0, top-left anchor shifts 84->88). Once selected the hopModel applies exactly (RAM+pixel confirmed at ticks 20206 [-3 phase] and 20215 [+1 phase]).

BAYLEEF.note: verified: diff 17px (frame0)/22px (frame1) out of ~300-400 opaque pixels, confined to screen (105-110,25-26) - RESOLVED this session, see mechanism.statusIconOverlap: this is BAYLEEF's own status-ailment indicator sprite drawing on top of its icon's corner, not an extraction bug. Never selected in this turn's script (cursor never reaches BAYLEEF), so no hop variant needed for it.

faintedIconPalette.verdict: REFUTED this session: there is NO separate hardware palette for a fainted mon's icon sprite. RAM-dumped OBJ palette slot 5 (ONIX's icon, tick 20150) is byte-for-byte (accounting for the GBA's 5-bit-per-channel expansion) IDENTICAL to `graphics/pokemon/icon_palettes/icon_palette_2.pal` (gMonIconPaletteIndices[SPECIES_ONIX]=2's own normal table) - the exact same table already banked in src/assets/gen/party-mon-icons.json's ONIX entry. `PARTY_PAL_FAINTED` (party_menu.c:1171,2244-2256) only ever loads into the BOX PANEL's own BG palette (`LoadPartyBoxPalette`, offset computed via `BG_PLTT_ID(GetWindowAttribute(...))` - background palette memory, never touched by the icon's own OBJ-palette sprite). The earlier '~400/1024px mismatch, confirming the palette-swap theory' finding was actually explained by the UNMODELED selected-icon bounce hop (hopModel above) shifting ONIX's icon position by up to 4px - not a palette difference at all. No new palette table needed; party-mon-icons.json's existing ONIX entry (icon.png's own embedded palette) is correct and sufficient, now composite-verified (see docs/party-menu-notes.md).
